benefits: Feeds spreadsheet data into systems that expect XML: SOAP APIs, config importers and legacy software.
Custom root and row element names let the output match the schema your system requires.
Automatic escaping of &, < and > keeps the document well-formed every time.
Runs fully in the browser, so sensitive rows are never uploaded anywhere.

faqs.a: The output is plain UTF-8 XML with an XML declaration, one root element, and one row element per data row. Field elements use your header names, sanitized into valid XML names.
faqs.q: What does the generated XML look like?

faqs.a: Root and row names must be valid XML names: start with a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscore, dot or hyphen. The tool blocks conversion and shows a warning until both names are valid.
Header text is sanitized: spaces become underscores and illegal characters are removed. A header like "First Name" becomes <First_Name>. Empty headers become field1, field2 and so on.
faqs.q: How are messy header names handled?

faqs.a: Yes, & becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, and quotes become " and '. The document always stays well-formed.
No. All values become text content inside elements. If you need typed values or attributes, use the JSON, XML & CSV converter, which supports XML attributes.

howTo: Paste your CSV, upload a .csv file, or press Sample.
Leave the delimiter on Auto or pick it manually.
Set the root element name and the row element name, for example rows and row.
Keep First row is header on if your CSV has column names.
Press Download to save data.xml, or Copy to paste it elsewhere.
keyFacts: Emits a well-formed XML document with an XML declaration and UTF-8 encoding.
One row element per CSV data row; field elements come from the header row.
Root and row element names are fully customizable and validated as legal XML names.
Special characters are escaped automatically, so output always parses.
Choose pretty-printed or compact output with one toggle.

labels.invalidName: Root and row names must be valid XML names: start with a letter or underscore.

limitations: Flat structure only; nested elements are not generated.
All values are text; no type information or attributes are emitted.
Duplicate header names produce duplicate element names.
Very large inputs (tens of MB) can make the browser tab sluggish.

csv-to-xml.quickAnswer: Paste or upload a CSV and get a well-formed XML document. Each row becomes an element with child elements named after your headers, and you can customize the root and row tag names to match the schema your system expects. Download data.xml or copy it directly.
csv-to-xml.tagline: Turn CSV rows into clean, well-formed XML.
csv-to-xml.workedExample:
Input CSV:
name,age,city
Aarav Sharma,25,Mumbai

With root = rows and row = row, the pretty output is:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rows>
  <row>
    <name>Aarav Sharma</name>
    <age>25</age>
    <city>Mumbai</city>
  </row>
</rows>

1 record, 3 fields, 8 lines of XML.
